new_statements.quote: Chaque syllabe porte un ton, aussi nécessaire à son identification que l'initiale ou la finale. Il n'existe pas dans la chaîne de position où toutes les distinctions tonales sont neutralisées, comme dans le cas du "ton neutre" du pékinois. [...] Le système tonal présente un paradigme de huit unités en syllabe PP, et de sept seulement en syllabe NPP, où les tons 3 et 4 sont confondus. (p. 29) [...] Dans tous les autres contextes [...] T7 se réalise comme un ton ponctuel bas qui donne une impression auditive semblable à celle du "ton neutre" pékinois lorsqu'il suit une syllabe au quatrième ton. (p. 32)
new_statements.translation: Every syllable carries a tone, which is as necessary to its identification as the initial or the final. There is no position in the chain where all tonal distinctions are neutralised, as is the case with the 'neutral tone' of Pekingese. [...] The tonal system has a paradigm of eight units in PP (pre-pausal) syllables and only seven in NPP (non-pre-pausal) syllables, where tones 3 and 4 merge. (p. 29) [...] In all other contexts [...] T7 is realised as a low punctual tone that gives an auditory impression similar to that of the Pekingese 'neutral tone' when it follows a fourth-tone syllable. (p. 32)

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, no existing statement; all seven sources read earlier were silent on stress). Dell 1981 adds a first-hand prosodic statement for Dali Bai, but it is a tone statement only (every syllable fully toned, no neutral-tone/atonic positions); it makes no claim about word stress, so it neither supplies nor contradicts a stress placement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Dali (Southern) Bai is described as a syllable-tone language: eight tones before pause, seven elsewhere (T3/T4 merge in non-pre-pausal syllables); every syllable bears a full tone and Dell states explicitly that there is no position in which tonal contrasts are neutralised the way Beijing Mandarin neutral-tone (atonic, unstressed) syllables are. The whole phonology chapter (pp. 21-35: preliminaries, initials, finals, tones, notes) and the transcription conventions of chap. 3 (pp. 37-43) contain no statement about word stress, accent or prominence; the only conditioning of tone realisation is positional (pre-pausal vs non-pre-pausal), not accentual. The word 'accent' occurs only in chap. 1 (pp. 12-18) in the sense of a regional (Yunnanese/rural) accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Not stress exceptions: T3/T4 contrast maintained only in pre-pausal syllables and lexically (classes a/b/c, p. 30-31); T7 non-initially sounds like a Pekingese neutral tone (p. 32); tone durations measured (T8 shortest 15 cs.. T7 longest 39 cs, p. 33).
new_statements.identity_note: Dell 1981 describes the Bai of Dà-lǐ 大理 (data collected 1966-67 from one 25-year-old speaker, G.K.C., from a locality near Dali), i.e. the Dali/Southern dialect in Xu & Zhao's classification = Glottolog Southern Bai (sout2730); chapters 5-6 compare it with Jianchuan (Central) and Bijiang (Northern) Bai and with Chinese.

tone_statements.quote: 喜洲美坝村位于大理洱海以西，距离大理古城约 17 公里，距周城约 2 公里。周围都是白族村落，村民之间通白语。根据汪锋（2006）提出的白语亲缘分群特征，美坝白语属白语东部方言，近周城方言。美坝白语有 23 个声母，20 个韵母，8 个声调。本文研究美坝白语的声调系统，如下表 1 所列 T1-T8。根据声调是否带有特殊发声类型而列出 “松”或“紧”，紧调是带有特殊发声类型的声调，一共有三个紧调：T2、T6、T7，其他都是普通发声类型的松调，下文都标明声调的松紧类，标注如“松调 T1”、“紧调 T2”等。
tone_statements.translation: Meiba village (Xizhou) lies west of Erhai in Dali, about 17 km from Dali old town and about 2 km from Zhoucheng. It is surrounded by Bai villages and the villagers speak Bai among themselves. By Wang Feng's (2006) subgrouping features Meiba Bai belongs to the Eastern branch of Bai, close to the Zhoucheng dialect. Meiba Bai has 23 initials, 20 finals and 8 tones. This paper studies the tone system of Meiba Bai, T1-T8 as listed in Table 1. Tones are marked 'lax' or 'tense' according to whether they carry a special phonation type; tense tones are those with special phonation, three in all: T2, T6, T7; the others are lax tones with plain phonation; below every tone is labelled for its lax/tense class, e.g. 'lax T1', 'tense T2'.

tone_statements.n_tones: 8 (T1 33, T2 53 tense, T3 31, T4 55, T5 35, T6 44 tense, T7 21 tense, T8 42)

tone_statements.quote: Like in Mandarin Chinese, a vowel and a tone are necessary in a syllable of Bai. [...] In Bai dialects, special phonation types have been found, such as tense, breathy or harsh (Li & Edmondson 1990, Edmondson & Li 1994), and they contrast with modal sounds. Following Xu & Zhao (1984), a tone category was assigned for each distinctive phonation type. [...] 8. Zhoucheng Bai [...] Tones (7): [table, linearised] Modal tone 55 | 33 | 31 | 35 — Non-modal tone 44 [tense] | 42 [laryngealized] | 21 [breathy]. Table 21: The tonal system of ZC. Language consultant: Yang Guohong 楊國紅. Born in 1952 in the Zhoucheng village.
